__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | category = Recipes for dessert | servings = 6–10 | time = Prep: ~60 minutes
Baking: ~60 minutes | difficulty = 3 | image = [[Image:Pecan pie.jpg|300px]] }}{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Desserts]] This is a recipe for a traditional '''pecan pie''', which is a popular [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] in many parts of the southern USA. Pecan pies are often served on holidays and special occasions, most commonly at Christmas and Thanksgiving Day meals. ==Ingredients== ===Pie crust=== *2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|grams]]) pastry (or all-purpose) [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] *1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] (6 grams) [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] *2 teaspoons (8 grams) [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] *{{fraction|1|2}} cup (115 grams) unsalted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] *{{fraction|1|4}} cup (50 grams) Crisco vegetable [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]] (or lard) *{{fraction|1|2}} cup (115 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|milliliters]]) very cold [[Cookbook:Water|water]] ===Pie filling=== *6 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] (85 grams) unsalted [[cookbook:butter|butter]] *1 packed cup (200 grams) dark [[cookbook:Brown_Sugar|brown sugar]] *{{fraction|1|2}} teaspoon (3 grams) [[cookbook:salt|salt]] *{{fraction|3|4}} cup (250 grams) light [[Cookbook:Corn_Syrup|corn syrup]] *1 tablespoon (13 grams) [[cookbook:vanilla|vanilla extract]] *1 tablespoon (45 milliliters) [[Cookbook:Bourbon|bourbon]] whiskey or dark [[Cookbook:Rum|rum]] *2 cups (475 milliliters) [[cookbook:pecan|pecans]] *3 large [[cookbook:egg|eggs]] ==Procedure== ===Roasting the pecans=== #Spread whole pecans onto a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]] and [[Cookbook:Roasting|roast]] in a 350°F (175°C) oven for 10 minutes. #Allow the pecans to cool, then [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] coarsely. ===Pie Crust=== [[File:Empty blind baked pie crust.png|alt=Par-baked pie crust|thumb|The pie crust needs to be baked before the filling is added. Otherwise, the filling will soak into the crust and make it soggy.|290x290px]] #[[Cookbook:Dice|Dice]] butter into cubes and place butter and shortening in freezer for 20–30 minutes. #Combine the flour, sugar, and salt in a [[Cookbook:Food Processor|food processor]] and pulse several times to mix. #Add the butter and shortening, and pulse 8–12 times until the butter is the size of peas. #Mix the water and vinegar together. #With the processor running, pour the water/vinegar mixture down the feed tube and pulse until the mixture begins to come together into a [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. #Dump the dough out onto a board and press it together, forming the dough into a disk. #Wrap the dough in [[Cookbook:Plastic Wrap|plastic wrap]] and refrigerate for approximately 30 minutes. #[[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] dough on a well-floured board into a circle, rolling from the center out, turning and flouring so the dough does not stick to the board. #Roll the dough onto the rolling pin and transfer to a 9-inch [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie dish]]. #Mold the dough into the pie dish, pushing the dough into the corners. #Dock the bottom of the crust with a fork to help prevent the crust from puffing up when baking. #Place the pie shell in the freezer for 30 minutes. #Line the pie shell with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]] and fill with pie weights (or dried beans). #Place the pie dish on a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] and [[Cookbook:Bake|bake]] the pie shell for 20 minutes at 375°F (190°C) on the middle oven rack. #Remove pie weights by lifting out the parchment paper. Continue to bake pie shell for another 10 minutes. ===Pie Filling=== [[File:Stirring pecan pie filling.png|alt=Metal bowl with pecan pie filling and a wooden spoon|thumb|The pie filling is cooked in the top of a double-boiler, or in a metal bowl set over a pan of simmering water. The bottom of the bowl should not touch the hot water.|290x290px]] While the pie crust is baking, proceed to making the filling: #In a medium [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium heat, melt the butter. #Stir in the brown sugar and salt until combined. #Add the corn syrup, and bring the mixture up to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]], stirring occasionally so the filling does not burn on the bottom of the saucepan. #Continue to stir and allow the mixture to boil for 1 minute, then remove from heat. #Stir in the bourbon, vanilla, and chopped pecans. #Allow the mixture to cool for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. #Beat the eggs and stir them into the cooled mixture a little at a time. ===Baking=== #Reduce oven temperature to 350°F (175°C). #Pour the filling into the hot pie crust. #Place the pie dish still on a cookie sheet back into the oven on the lower 3rd over rack; if you have a pie shield, put it in place to prevent the edges of the crust from getting too brown. #[[cookbook:Bake|Bake]] at 350°F (175°C) for 45 minutes, filling should still be slightly jiggly when removed from oven. #Allow pie to cool on a cooling rack for 2–4 hours. Pie will cool to doneness. #Serve warm with [[cookbook:Whipped Cream|whipped cream]] or vanilla [[cookbook:Ice Cream|ice cream]]. ==Notes, tips, and variations== *Don't skip the pecan roasting process. Roasting the pecans greatly enhances the flavor and texture of the nuts. It is best to roast the pecans whole and then chop after roasting. Roasting the nuts whole helps to ensure even roasting of the nuts. *If you prefer the look of a lighter-colored filling, you can substitute light brown sugar for the dark brown sugar. ==Warnings== *Filling will be extremely hot immediately after the pie is taken from the oven and is continuing to cook to doneness as it cools, so let it cool for at least an hour before you cut into it. ==See also== * [[Cookbook:Chocolate Bourbon Pecan Pie]] * [[Cookbook:Layered Pecan Pie]] [[Category:Recipes using pecan]] [[Category:Southern U.S. recipes]] [[Category:Inexpensive recipes]] [[Category:Recipes for pecan pie]] [[Category:Recipes using butter]] [[Category:Recipes using egg]] [[Category:Recipes for dessert]] [[Category:Recipes using bourbon]] [[Category:Recipes using dark brown sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using corn syrup]] [[Category:Recipes using pie dough]] [[Category:Recipes using wheat flour]] [[Category:Recipes using lard]] [[Category:Recipes for pie dough]]
